question: Should OpenClaw permanently support this three-method public plugin approval API and its corresponding Gateway/native-client contract for external verification ceremonies?
rationale: The patch is not merely a bounded implementation: it establishes durable plugin, protocol, and client compatibility commitments with security-sensitive approval semantics.

options.title: Adopt the public contract
options.body: Confirm the RFC-shaped API as supported, require a current-main rebase and green generated-doc/SDK gates, then continue normal merge review.

options.title: Narrow to an internal seam
options.body: Keep the host-owned approval design but avoid exporting the current broad plugin SDK surface until a smaller supported contract is chosen.

options.title: Defer core support
options.body: Keep the external-verification capability in an owner plugin or companion project until OpenClaw maintainers sponsor a stable core API.

recommendation.title: Adopt the public contract
recommendation.body: Confirm the RFC-shaped API as supported, require a current-main rebase and green generated-doc/SDK gates, then continue normal merge review.

likelyOwner.reason: Related approval API review activity makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the host/plugin contract decision.
